chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who performed Ziyarah to the House, circled the House, and [circled] between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then returned. His eyelids overpowered him during the circling, so he slept until morning. He said: 'A sheep is due from him.' This does not contradict what the first report contained from his statement, except if he had left Mecca, because that report is applicable to one who left Mecca and passed the pass of the Madaniyyun. Indeed, it is permissible for him to sleep, and the state as we described it indicates that.

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Safa and Al-Marwah (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.شَاةٌ: A sheep (a specific type of sacrificial offering)
key_terms.عَقَبَةَ الْمَدَنِيِّينَ: The pass of the Madaniyyun (a specific location near Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a pilgrim who falls asleep during Tawaf al-Ziyarah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a pilgrim who falls asleep during Tawaf incurs the penalty of a sheep (shath), a ruling consistent with earlier reports but specifically contextualized for those who have exited Mecca past the pass of the Madaniyyun. This distinction highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of rituals when interrupted by sleep, emphasizing that the penalty applies when the pilgrim is still within the sacred precincts or has just exited, rather than after fully departing the ritual zone.
